Thanks for the demo today — appreciate the crisp walkthrough. I captured a few technical asks that my engineers want validated before we move to procurement: 

- Auth & SDK: we need a recommended auth flow for our backend services (short-lived tokens vs mTLS). Our infra team prefers token rotation via our KMS and SSO integration.
- Routing: we will have two classes of traffic — low-latency interactive chat (~40% of calls) and high-throughput batch reranking/embeddings (~60%). We need a routing plan and how Redwood supports per-route model variants.
- Structured output / tool calling: we plan to use tool-calls to retrieve account balances and a small set of internal APIs. We need guidance on safe tool sandboxing and structured schema enforcement.
- Embeddings & reranker: expected 200k embeddings/month initially; reranker queries ~800 QPS at peak (sub-second targets). Need recommendations for batching and cost tradeoffs.
- Dedicated capacity sizing: baseline steady-state traffic ~120 QPS of gen calls (avg 25 tokens/generated response), peak bursts up to 2x for short windows (10-15 mins). We want autoscale recommendations and concurrency limits to avoid head-of-line blocking.

I attached a short spreadsheet (FinLytics_Integration_Reqs.xlsx) with traffic patterns and a sample conversation. Can you confirm whether Redwood can meet a 95th latency target of <200ms for the interactive path and propose a preliminary sizing and MLP for a POC?

Next step: can we schedule a 60–90 min technical deep-dive with your solutions engineer and our infra team next week? Emily

3) 2-week integration: full SDK integration, tool-calling tests, and reranker evaluation.
4) UAT + handoff.

Emily / Markus — quick technical sketch based on the spreadsheet and the numbers Emily provided. This is intentionally conservative; we will validate during the spike.

Assumptions:
- Interactive generation path: 120 QPS steady, avg response ~25 tokens (model: 7B–13B family). Target 95th < 200ms.
- Reranker/embeddings path: 800 QPS peak for retrieval/rerank (these are short calls, ~5–10 tokens for the model step; heavy on embedding lookups).
- Burst windows: 2x traffic for 10–15 mins.

Sizing recommendations (initial dedicated pool):
- Baseline reserved: 4 GPUs (NVIDIA A100-class or equivalent) with optimized kernels. Expect this to handle the steady 120 QPS interactive + background embedding jobs with aggressive batching.
- Autoscale policy: scale up to 8 GPUs when observed GPU utilization > 70% for rolling 3-minute window, scale down when < 45% for 10 minutes. This handles 2x bursts with headroom and keeps costs predictable.
- Concurrency limits: set per-GPU concurrency at ~12 model streams for generation (depends on model size and quantization). For rerank/embedding workers, use dedicated workers with higher batching (per-GPU concurrency 24) to maximize throughput.
- Queues & timeouts: route interactive calls through a low-latency queue (max queue depth 40ms target), with hard timeout at 2s to avoid blocking. Reranker/embedding jobs go to high-throughput queue with batching window up to 50ms.
- KV caching & prefix caching: enable per-session KV cache for chat-like flows to reduce token compute on common prefixes.
- Quantization & model variant: recommend int8/4 quantized variant for reranker and embedding paths to increase concurrency; keep a higher-fidelity (int8 HF or float16) for the interactive path if quality matters.

Cost/latency tradeoffs: using higher batching for rerankers will lower cost but increase p99 latency — we can tune target batching window during the spike.

Attachments: I exported a simple sizing template (redwood-sizing-template.csv) and linked a sample autoscale policy in our drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3cSizingTemplate

Let me know if this aligns with your infra constraints. Happy to present these numbers during the technical deep-dive and run a one-week spike to validate behavior and iterate.

- Ben Carter
